components.css: .ds-day-slot { position: relative; width: 64px; min-height: 62px; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #8fd1b0; background: #eef8f2; padding: 6px 5px 9px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; font-family: 'Avenir Next', sans-serif; color: #2c1e1b; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-day-slot:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: #c84359; } .ds-slot-top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 0.74rem; font-weight: 800; } .ds-slot-top small { font-size: 0.56rem; color: #7a605a; } .ds-slot-badge { font-size: 0.66rem; font-weight: 800; color: #246a49; text-align: center; } .ds-slot-bar { position: absolute; bottom: 3px; left: 4px; right: 4px; height: 3.5px; background: rgba(44,30,27,0.08); border-radius: 99px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-slot-bar > div { height: 100%; background: #246a49; }

narrative.northStar: The Tactile Stationery Desk Planner & Calibrated Sticker Cradle
narrative.overview: Rather than presenting On-the-Job Training (OJT) hours as a cold corporate spreadsheet or generic SaaS KPI grid, this system embodies a physical Japanese stationery desk diary open across a dotted craft mat. The left page serves as a ruled accounting proof sheet where every step of the 480-hour formula is derived transparently, while the right page houses a four-month recessed calendar cradle where each scheduled workday sits as a physical paper slot with a proportional capacity bar and bespoke SVG sticker stamp.
keyCharacteristics: Open two-page desk planner spread bound by a center spiral ring column on desktop viewports.
Warm oat-and-strawberry stationery palette (#FAF5EE paper over #F3EAE0 dotted desk mat) with high-contrast espresso ink (#2C1E1B).
Proportional capacity bars inside every calendar day slot showing rendered hours out of the 8.8h daily maximum.
Custom-drawn inline SVG stamps in a unified 1.5px–2.2px stroke weight with zero unicode emojis.

rules.name: The Semantic Stamp Ink Rule
rules.body: Every attendance state owns one dedicated ink-and-wash pair across the ledger dot, the stamp palette button, the calendar slot background, and the bottom capacity bar. Never mix status hues across unrelated UI chrome.

rules.name: The Tabular Chronometer Rule
rules.body: Every element displaying hours, days, percentages, dates, or clock times must apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so vertical columns and live updates never jitter.

rules.name: The Soft Paper Elevation Rule
rules.body: Shadows always carry a vertical offset and soft blur tinted with warm umber (rgba(68, 41, 34, ...)). Zero-blur hard offset block shadows are never used.

dos: Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every hour, workday count, percentage, and clock-out time.
Do draw all icons and attendance stamps as inline SVGs with 1.5px–2.2px strokes anchored to the espresso and stamp ink palette.
Do keep day editing inline inside the planner page via the Day Inspector slip or one-click Sticker Stamp mode.
donts: Don't place kickers, eyebrows, or numbered badges (01 / 02) above headings.
Don't use unicode emojis or stock icon fonts anywhere in the interface.
Don't use colored left or right accent borders thicker than 1px on cards or callouts.
